reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Welcoming UN AI resolutions and Pact
themes.definition: Welcoming UN outcomes on AI and digital cooperation: the Pact for the Future, Global Digital Compact, and the first GA resolution on AI.
themes.inclusion: Include passages welcoming UN agreements, resolutions or compacts that address AI.
themes.exclusion: Exclude UN reform or Secretary-General selection remarks without AI content.
themes.boundary_cases: A summary of a UN summit agenda naming AI as one item counts here if the UN outcome is the focus.

examples.quote: the first-ever resolution on artificial intelligence, to promote safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for sustainable development
ensuring that we make artificial intelligence, a technology that benefits all

themes.label: AI accelerating development and state capacity
themes.definition: AI and digital transition as opportunities to accelerate development and improve state capacities.
themes.inclusion: Include claims that AI can accelerate development or serve sustainable development.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages focused only on access gaps.
themes.boundary_cases: Conditional benefit statements ('only if we bridge the divide') are coded here and AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: The digital transition and artificial intelligence also offer new opportunities to accelerate development and improve the capacities of our states.

themes.label: Bridge divide via technology sharing
themes.definition: Conditioning AI's benefits on bridging the digital divide, technology sharing and building developing-country capacities.
themes.inclusion: Include calls for technology sharing, capacity-building or bridging the digital divide in connection with AI.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general development finance calls unrelated to technology.
themes.boundary_cases: If only the gap is described without a remedy, prefer AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: bridge the digital divide, facilitate technology sharing, and build the capacities of developing countries

value.rationale: Djibouti's AI references are brief and multilateral: welcoming UN AI outcomes and framing AI as a development opportunity conditional on bridging the divide; most of each passage concerns other topics.
